what: Defects found in the 60 OFFICIAL NPHIES sample messages themselves. These are faults in the published samples, not rules a HIS must follow. A hospital whose message was rejected after being copied from one of these files needs to know the sample was wrong.
howToReadThis: severity fatal: the file cannot be parsed or is not the message type it claims to be. Nothing downstream works.
severity major: the file parses, but an element is misnamed, mis-shaped or unresolvable, so data is silently lost or a strict validator rejects it.
severity minor: the file is usable; the defect affects narrative linkage, identifier reuse, tolerant-parser-only behaviour or provenance.
confidence low or medium means the finding is recorded with its doubt stated in confidenceReason. Read that field before acting on it.
evidence is the exact text as it appears in the file. location gives line/col/xpath/jsonPath where they apply.

basis, where present, quotes the Confluence row the sample contradicts. Absence of basis means the finding rests on the base standard (RFC 8259, XML 1.0, SOAP 1.2, FHIR R4, HL7 v2.5.1, IHE ITI) alone.
Every finding here was reproduced against the file on disk by the check named in verifiedBy.

defects.description: The file is not RFC 8259 JSON. It carries 8 line(s) of "//"-style annotation comments (written as "///" or "/////") appended after values. JSON has no comment syntax, so the first one terminates parsing.
defects.impact: Python json.loads, JavaScript JSON.parse, Jackson, System.Text.Json and the HAPI FHIR JSON parser all reject the file as published with "Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 89 column 52 (char 3260)" or the equivalent. A HIS that downloads the sample and feeds it to a stock parser fails before any FHIR validation runs, which can be misread as a problem in the HIS.
defects.workaround: Delete everything from the first unquoted "//" to end of line on each affected line, then re-parse. A JSON5 / JSONC / relaxed reader (json5, Newtonsoft with CommentHandling.Ignore, VS Code jsonc) accepts the file unchanged, so the file may appear valid in an editor while failing in the integration pipeline. Do not ship the comments in a live message.
defects.verifiedBy: json.loads() on the file as published; then json.loads() after stripping unquoted // to end-of-line

defects.description: The file is an escaped-string dump, not HL7 v2 wire format. Two problems, both visible in the raw bytes: (a) six segments end with the literal two characters backslash + r (bytes 0x5C 0x72) before the real line break, instead of a segment terminator; (b) MSH-2 reads ^~\\& with a doubled backslash (five characters) instead of the four-character ^~\&.
defects.impact: An HL7 v2 parser reads MSH-2 as declaring the escape character to be backslash and the subcomponent separator to be backslash, which corrupts component parsing for the whole message; it also sees a trailing literal "\r" as data on the last field of every segment. The message cannot be replayed as-is over MLLP or a file feed.
defects.workaround: Unescape before use: replace the literal two-character \r with a real CR (0x0D) segment terminator, and set MSH-2 to the four characters ^~\&. ADT_sample08.txt in the same folder is already clean and can be used as the reference message.
defects.verifiedBy: byte inspection: 6 occurrences of 0x5C 0x72 and MSH-2 = ^~\\& in these two files; 0 occurrences and MSH-2 = ^~\& in ADT_sample08.txt

defects.sampleFile: golden/SOAP/ITI-18/1 nphies ITI18 RegistryStoredQueryResponse v4.9beta1 - Returns Discharge Summary DocumentEntry - Kopie.xml
defects.description: The document element is written <soap:envelope> / </soap:envelope> in lower case. XML element names are case sensitive, and SOAP 1.2 (and 1.1) define the document element as "Envelope" with a capital E in the envelope namespace. The child elements soap:Header and soap:Body in the same files are correctly cased, so only the outermost element is affected.
defects.impact: The file is well-formed XML but is not a SOAP envelope. A SOAP 1.2 processor that receives it raises env:VersionMismatch (or, in many stacks, a "not a valid SOAP message / unexpected element" error) and never reaches the ITI-18 payload. A HIS using these two files as the reference shape for its ITI-18 response handler will build a parser against an element name that never appears on the wire.
defects.workaround: Read them as "soap:Envelope". The 17 other golden SOAP samples, including the two matching ITI-18 request files in the same folder, all use <soap:Envelope>; use one of those as the envelope reference.
defects.verifiedBy: expat parse of all 19 golden SOAP files, recording the document element name; 17 return soap:Envelope, these 2 return soap:envelope

defects.description: The FHIR R4 element ServiceRequest.occurrencePeriod is spelled "occurencePeriod" with one "r" at 5 location(s) in this file. The first occurrence in this file uses the correct spelling, so the two spellings sit side by side in one bundle.
defects.impact: The period is dropped by a lenient FHIR parser and rejected by a strict one. Across the golden set the misspelling outnumbers the correct spelling 33 to 5, so an integrator sampling these files will most likely copy the wrong name.
defects.workaround: Use "occurrencePeriod" (two r). Search the whole file, not just the first hit.
defects.verifiedBy: literal count of "occurencePeriod" vs "occurrencePeriod" across all 22 golden FHIR bundles (33 vs 5)
defects.note: The 27-01-2026 and 09-02-2026 re-issues corrected only the FIRST occurrence in each file and left the rest, which is why both spellings appear here.

defects.description: Observation.effective[x] is written "effectivedateTime" with a lower-case "d" at 3 location(s), on Observation resources claiming the AdditionalOrderInformation profile. The FHIR R4 choice-type element is "effectiveDateTime".
defects.impact: The effective date/time of the additional order information is dropped by a lenient parser and rejected by a strict one. Choice-type element names are case sensitive in FHIR JSON; "effectivedateTime" matches no element.
defects.workaround: Use "effectiveDateTime" (capital D). The value itself is a well-formed FHIR dateTime and needs no change.
defects.verifiedBy: literal count of "effectivedateTime" vs "effectiveDateTime" across all 22 golden FHIR bundles (12 vs 3, the 3 being an unrelated element in the Raqeeb medication bundles)

defects.description: Reference.identifier is encoded as a JSON array at 5 location(s) in this file, on Reference-typed elements such as subject, author, custodian, sender, focus, practitioner, organization, encounter, party, authorizingPrescription and context. Reference.identifier is 0..1 Identifier in FHIR R4, so in FHIR JSON it must be a single object.
defects.impact: A strict FHIR R4 JSON parser raises "Found array in element identifier of type Identifier" and fails the bundle. A HIS building from these samples will produce Reference blocks that do not round-trip through a stock R4 library.
defects.workaround: Emit the single Identifier object: "identifier": { "system": ..., "value": ... }. Because all 21 parseable golden FHIR bundles use the array form without exception, confirm with NPHIES whether the platform in fact accepts the array before changing a working integration.
defects.verifiedBy: JSON type of Reference.identifier at every Reference-shaped object across all 21 parseable golden FHIR bundles (array in 21 of 21 files)
defects.confidenceReason: The FHIR R4 base cardinality is unambiguous, but the Confluence guidance only says the sub-element "SHALL contain exactly the same Identifier as in the referenced resource (“identifier” element)" without stating cardinality, and the golden set is unanimous. This may be an accepted NPHIES encoding rather than an oversight, so it is recorded as medium confidence.

defects.impact: ClinicalDocument/id becomes the XDS DocumentEntry.uniqueId, which must identify exactly one document, and setId identifies one document lineage. As published, these six files claim to be six versions of one document. Submitting two of them unchanged to the same registry is a uniqueId collision and the second submission is rejected. The samples are still usable as structure references; only the identifier values must not be copied.

defects.description: Segments are separated by CRLF (0x0D 0x0A). HL7 v2 uses a bare CR (0x0D) as the segment terminator; the LF is not part of the message. The file contains 6 CRLF pairs and no bare CR.

defects.description: The OID 2.16.840.1.113883.3.3731.1.2.2.11111111111110 appears here in an instance-identifier position. The same OID string is simultaneously normative in one and only one place - the xmlns:nphies namespace declaration on a CDA document root, where the spec states it as a SHALL and all 16 golden CDA files emit it byte-identically. spec-build/constants.json quarantines the OID outside that one exempt context on the pattern rule "an arc contains a run of four or more identical digits" (11111111111110). The sample gives the reader no marker distinguishing the normative use from the placeholder use.
defects.impact: An integrator who copies the value here submits a document or query naming a repository/document authority that is not theirs. Because the identical string is genuinely required in xmlns:nphies, a search-and-replace across the file will also break the namespace declaration.
defects.workaround: Replace this occurrence with your own assigned OID and leave xmlns:nphies untouched. constants.json#quarantined carries the exemptContexts entry describing exactly which position is normative.
defects.verifiedBy: scanned every golden sample for each of the 11 quarantined OIDs in spec-build/constants.json and recorded the enclosing element/attribute
defects.confidenceReason: Sample data in a sample file is expected, so this is not reported as an error in the file. It is recorded because this specific OID is both normative and placeholder depending on position, which is a documented ambiguity rather than a judgement call.

defects.description: The WS-Addressing MessageID carries "uuid:a54d6aa5-d40d-43f9-88c5-b4633d873bdc". The registered URN namespace for a UUID is "urn:uuid:" (RFC 4122); "uuid:" alone is not a registered URI scheme. All four ITI-43 samples use the short form while all 15 other golden SOAP samples, including the ITI-18 request/response pair carrying the same UUID value, use "urn:uuid:".
defects.impact: wsa:MessageID is typed xs:anyURI and must be an absolute IRI. scanMethodology: All 62 files under spec-source/golden/ were enumerated; the 60 that are message samples (the .zip and .xlsx carry no message) were audited. Checks actually run, each re-executed against the file on disk rather than taken from spec-build/golden.json: (1) JSON well-formedness with RFC 8259 json.loads, then again after stripping unquoted "//" to end-of-line, to separate comment-only damage from structural damage. (2) XML well-formedness with expat on all 35 XML files, recording the document element name, every element name and every attribute name. (3) Identifier character check: every JSON key in all 21 parseable FHIR bundles and every XML element and attribute name in all 35 XML files tested against [A-Za-z0-9_.:-]; separately a full non-ASCII census of the golden set (0x2019 right single quote 29x, 0x2193 downwards arrow 10x, 0x2013 en dash 9x, Arabic letters 13x) with each occurrence classified as identifier or human-readable text. Only one non-ASCII character in the entire golden set sits inside an identifier. (4) FHIR element-name spelling: every distinct JSON key across the bundles (157 keys) reviewed; occurencePeriod/occurrencePeriod/occur<U+0642>encePeriod and effectivedateTime/effectiveDateTime counted per file and per line. (5) FHIR JSON shape: HumanName.given, Address.line, MessageHeader.focus, Reference.identifier, ContactPoint.rank, MedicationRequest.groupIdentifier checked against FHIR R4 base cardinality and datatype, then cross-checked against the Confluence row where one exists. (6) Reference integrity: every Reference.reference in every FHIR bundle resolved against bundle fullUrls, ResourceType/id pairs and the containing resource's contained[] ids; every #-prefixed CDA originalText/reference/@value resolved against the @ID attributes in the same document; every XDS Association sourceObject/targetObject and Document/@id resolved against the ExtrinsicObject and RegistryPackage ids in the same submission. (7) Profile URLs: every meta.profile value checked against constants.json#fhirProfiles.items - all resolved, no defect. (8) Placeholder OIDs: all 11 quarantined OIDs from constants.json searched across every sample, with the enclosing element/attribute recorded so the quarantine exemptContext could be applied. (9) Date formats: FHIR date/dateTime/instant against the R4 regexes, CDA effectiveTime/time/low/high against the HL7 TS pattern, XDS creationTime/serviceStartTime/serviceStopTime/submissionTime and the ITI-18 query time slots against the XDS DTM pattern. No date defect was found in any sample. (10) Cross-sample identity: ClinicalDocument/id, setId, code and versionNumber extracted from all 16 CDA files and grouped; XDS uniqueIds compared between the ITI-18/ITI-41/ITI-43 pairs. (11) HL7 v2 byte-level: segment terminators, MSH-2 encoding characters, MSH-12 version and character-set declaration read from the raw bytes. (12) Duplicate JSON keys and byte-order marks checked on every JSON file (none found).
